painting.title: THE LAST LANTERN ON THE MOOR ROAD AT NIGHT
painting.intro: A lonely stretch of rutted cart track crossing open moorland, where the last lit lantern of the fair's road stands on its tall iron post. It is full night, cold and clear, lit by the moon and by that one warm lamp.
bullets: The ground: the pale shape is a level track of bare trodden earth and grit with two shallow cart ruts, running from the left edge to the right edge and widening midway into a worn bay of bare earth in front of the lantern post. Everything off the track is dark heather and rough moor grass, clearly different from the pale earth. Nothing overhangs the track.
Far back on the left, a small still moor pool, black water catching a streak of moonlight, with rounded gorse bushes dark around it.

Far back on the right, a low heathery knoll with bare grey rock showing, hinting that the land rises that way. Beside it stands a single wind-bent thorn tree, bare and black, its crown swept hard to the right, with one more gorse bush at its foot.

Along the far side of the track, a waist-high drystone wall of grey lichened fieldstone in two runs, left and right. Between them, behind the lantern, is a gap where the wall has fallen, with a few tumbled stones in the grass.

Midway, at the far edge of the worn bay, the Last Lantern: a tall, slim black iron post on a footing of flat stones, with a curled bracket and one glass lantern at its top burning warm amber, the lantern held wholly below the skyline against the dark moor. Its light pools on the bare earth below and touches the nearest wall stones. It is the only lit lamp in the scene.
Further right along the far verge, a second, older iron post, rusted and leaning a little, with an empty bracket and no lantern, dark against the heather.

On the far verge at the left, a short, weathered, blank waystone and a mossy boulder mark where the track runs out of frame toward the fair. At the right the track runs out of frame between heather banks toward higher ground.

On the near side of the track, only low things: a knee-high broken length of drystone wall on the left, a low rounded boulder on the right, and low clumps of gorse and heather between them, all in dark silhouette with a thin moonlit rim.
painting.top: A night sky thick with stars over the dark, low line of the moor. Auros, the moon, is large, pale and nearly full in the upper left. Low on the left horizon beneath it, the fair is a small warm glow of tiny lights, far off. To the right the skyline rises a little, dark and empty.
